patches.before: The learner initially obtains q=40,p=60, demand point elasticity -1.5 (magnitude 1.5), and total surplus 1600 from two surplus areas of 800 each, then q=50,p=70 and total surplus 2500. They draw consistent price–quantity axes and explain a demand shift rather than movement along the old demand curve.
patches.after: The learner initially obtains q=40,p=60, demand point elasticity -1.5 (magnitude 1.5), and total surplus 1600 from two surplus areas of 800 each, then q=50,p=70 and total surplus 2500. They draw consistent price–quantity axes and explain a demand shift rather than movement along the old demand curve. They explain information about changed scarcity, incentives to expand supply, and coordination at the new price.
patches.reason: Restore the exact economic price-function aspect explicitly present in the German case expectation, original source and bilingual profile core.
